title: What Scripture Actually Means by Self-Control (It's Not Willpower)
caption:
What Scripture actually means by self-control. It's not a willpower problem.

You grit your teeth Monday morning and promise yourself this is the week. By Thursday night, tired and alone, you're back in the same tab you swore off. That's not a character flaw. Willpower runs like a battery, and it drains fastest right when you need it most.

Paul doesn't call it grit. He calls it fruit, something that grows out of a root, not something you manufacture by force. "The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control" (Galatians 5:22-23). It's not something you white-knuckle. It's what's left standing in a man walking with God.

Stop grading yourself only by what happens at midnight. Ask what fed the root that morning: did you open the Word before your phone, did you talk to God at all. A man who stays connected to the vine isn't gritting his teeth when the test comes.

Next time you fail, don't ask why you're weak. Ask what root you skipped feeding that morning.

theme: He runs his life — his impulses don't control him.
